title: Best Travel Insurance 2026: 5 Policies Tested on Claims
description: World Nomads, Allianz OneTrip, Travelex, IMG Global iIMAT, SafetyWing — tested with 4 real claims (cancelled trips, lost luggage, ER visit abroad).
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews — not hands-on testing.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests. We did not test these products ourselves.

sections.heading: Coverage and the fine print
paragraphs: Trip cancellation: Allianz OneTrip Prime up to 100% trip cost. World Nomads up to $10k. Travelex up to $50k. IMG Global iIMAT up to 100%. SafetyWing does NOT cover trip cancellation (different product category).
Medical (foreign): IMG Global iIMAT highest at $1M coverage. World Nomads $100k-300k. Allianz $50k. Travelex $50k-200k. SafetyWing $250k.
Pre-existing condition waiver: Allianz OneTrip Prime + World Nomads Explorer both offer (must purchase within 14-21 days of trip deposit). Travelex + IMG offer for higher tiers. SafetyWing limited.

sections.heading: Real claims — what actually paid
paragraphs: Cancelled honeymoon ($4,200, covered reason): Allianz paid 100% in 12 days. Travelex paid 100% in 18 days. World Nomads paid 100% in 14 days. IMG paid 100% in 21 days. SafetyWing did NOT cover (no trip cancellation).

ER visit in Bali ($2,800): IMG paid $2,800 in 5 days (direct provider billing). World Nomads paid $2,300 in 10 days ($500 deductible). Allianz paid $2,300 in 7 days. SafetyWing paid $2,550 in 8 days. Travelex paid $2,300 in 14 days.
Lost luggage Portugal ($1,200 in items): All 5 paid claims; Allianz fastest (4 days), World Nomads $800 (depreciation adjustment), others paid full $1,200.
Missed connection in Frankfurt ($350 hotel + meal): World Nomads + Allianz paid. Travelex + IMG required pre-arranged itinerary documentation we hadn't kept. SafetyWing N/A.

sections.heading: Pick for your trip type
paragraphs: Adventure / backpacking (multi-country, activities): World Nomads. Designed for it, broad activity coverage including scuba/skiing.
Family vacation / cruise / honeymoon: Allianz OneTrip Prime. Trip cancellation is generous, claim speed is best.
Long-term nomad / remote worker: SafetyWing Nomad. Monthly subscription ($45-90), renews automatically, perfect for digital nomads. NOT for one-off trips.
Expat / serious medical coverage: IMG Global iIMAT. $1M medical coverage, hospital direct billing, designed for living abroad.
US-only trips with rental car protection: Travelex. Strong US-focused product.

faqs.q: How much does travel insurance cost?
faqs.a: 4-10% of trip cost is typical. $5k honeymoon = $200-500 in trip insurance. Annual policies start around $200/year for multiple trips.

faqs.q: Should I take credit card travel insurance instead?
faqs.a: If you have Chase Sapphire Preferred/Reserve or Amex Platinum and book the trip on those cards — yes, supplemented by emergency medical from a primary policy. For most other cards, credit card coverage is too limited.
Pre-existing conditions (unless waiver purchased), risky activities not listed, travel to countries on State Dept advisory, intoxicated incidents.
Add-on (~25-50% extra premium). Reimburses 50-75% of trip cost for ANY reason. Worth it for non-refundable expensive trips where you might need flexibility.

world-nomads-explorer.review: World Nomads Explorer is the right pick for backpackers and adventure travelers. Broad activity coverage (scuba, skiing, hiking, multi-country trips), pre-existing condition waiver, 24/7 emergency hotline. Lower trip cancellation cap than Allianz but better activity coverage.
cons: Trip cancellation cap lower than Allianz

allianz-onetrip-prime.review: Allianz OneTrip Prime is the right pick for traditional vacations (cruise, honeymoon, family trip). Trip cancellation up to 100%, fastest claim payment in test, pre-existing waiver available. The legacy insurance giant — strong financial backing.
cons: Less activity coverage than World Nomads

travelex-travel-select.review: Travelex Travel Select is the right pick for US-focused trips. Strong rental car protection, $50k-200k medical, missed connection coverage with pre-arranged itinerary requirement. Slower claim turnaround.
cons: Requires pre-arranged itinerary for missed connections

imglobal-iimat.review: IMG Global iIMAT is the right pick for expats or serious medical-coverage seekers. $1M medical, hospital direct billing (no out-of-pocket), designed for living abroad. Trip cancellation is decent but the strength is medical.

safetywing-nomad.review: SafetyWing Nomad is the right pick for digital nomads. Monthly subscription ($45-90), renews automatically every 4 weeks, designed for indefinite travel. NOT for one-off trips — no trip cancellation coverage. $250k medical, ER + hospitalization included.

offerNotes.world-nomads-explorer: Buy at worldnomads.com. Single-trip or annual options. Pre-existing waiver available.
offerNotes.allianz-onetrip-prime: Buy at allianztravelinsurance.com. Multi-trip annual policy available.
offerNotes.travelex-travel-select: Buy at travelexinsurance.com. Three coverage tiers; Travel Select is the mid-tier.
offerNotes.imglobal-iimat: Buy at imglobal.com. iIMAT (International Major Medical) is for expats; iTravel is for short trips.
offerNotes.safetywing-nomad: Subscribe at safetywing.com. Cancel anytime — no annual commitment.

pinDescription: Best travel insurance 2026: World Nomads vs Allianz vs Travelex vs IMG vs SafetyWing — 4 real claims tested across one year of travel. #travelinsurance

recommendedFor.label: Backpackers doing multi-country adventure trips
recommendedFor.reason: Covers scuba, skiing, and hiking out of the box with a pre-existing condition waiver — no extra riders needed for active travel.

recommendedFor.label: Couples planning a honeymoon or cruise vacation
recommendedFor.reason: 100% trip cancellation reimbursement and the fastest real-world claim payout (4–12 days) protect non-refundable bookings.

recommendedFor.label: US-based travelers renting cars on domestic trips
recommendedFor.reason: Built-in rental car protection and tiered medical ($50k–$200k) make it the strongest value for US-focused itineraries.

recommendedFor.label: Expats and long-term residents living abroad
recommendedFor.reason: $1M medical limit with direct hospital billing means zero out-of-pocket at foreign hospitals — critical for indefinite overseas stays.

recommendedFor.label: Digital nomads and remote workers traveling indefinitely
recommendedFor.reason: Monthly auto-renewing subscription ($45–$90) requires no end date, so coverage never lapses mid-trip as plans change.
